etymologies.etymologyHTML:
From Middle English mone, mane, mān, (also as mene), from Old English *mān, *mǣn (“complaint; lamentation”), from Proto-West Germanic *mainu, from Proto-Germanic *mainō (“opinion; mind”).

Cognate with Old Frisian mēne (“opinion”), Old High German meina (“opinion”). Old English *mān, *mǣn is inferred from Old English mǣnan (“to complain over; grieve; mourn”). More at mean.

definitions.definition: A low, mournful cry of pain, sorrow or pleasure.

quote.citation: 1662, Richard Baxter, Now or never the holy, serious, diligent believer justified, encouraged, excited and directed, and the opposers and neglecters convinced by the light of Scripture and reason, pages 131 and 239:
quote.text: it shall be my daily grief and moan, that I am so dull, & do so little […] But if when all is done that we can do, you will leave us nothing but our tears and moans for self-destroyers, the sin is yours, and the suffering shall be yours.

quote.citation: 1660, John Ball, A treatise of divine meditation, page 255:
quote.text: to thee therefore oh Lord do I make my moan, to thee I render my humble petition, and pour out my soul which hath sinned against thee: Oh Lord, I beseech thee for thy infinite mercy in Jesus Christ, to take pity upon mee […]

definitions.definition: (transitive, now rare) To complain about; to bemoan, to bewail; to mourn. [from 13th c.]

quote.citation: 1596, Edmund Spenser, “Book VI, Canto VII”, in The Faerie Queene. […], London:  […]  [John Wolfe] for William Ponsonbie, →OCLC:
quote.text: Much did the Craven seeme to mone his case […].

quote.citation: 1708, Matthew Prior, the Turtle and the Sparrow
quote.text: Ye floods, ye woods, ye echoes, moan / My dear Columbo, dead and gone.

definitions.definition: (intransitive, now chiefly poetic) To grieve. [from 14th c.]
(intransitive) To make a moan or similar sound. [from 18th c.]

quote.citation: 1961 November 10, Joseph Heller, “The Soldier in White”, in Catch-22 […], New York, N.Y.: Simon and Schuster, →OCLC, page 169:
quote.text: They shared a common dread that he would begin moaning.

definitions.definition: (transitive) To say in a moan, or with a moaning voice. [from 19th c.]
(intransitive, colloquial) To complain; to grumble. [from 20th c.]
(transitive, obsolete) To distress (someone); to sadden. [15th–17th c.]
